title: HarvestLink
problem_statement: Independent restaurants and food co-ops spend 4-6 hours per week across phone calls and email threads sourcing fresh produce from local farms because there is no digital marketplace that aggregates availability, prices, and ordering for small farms within a 150-mile radius. Farms lose 15-25% of harvestable produce to waste because they have no reliable demand signal until the week of harvest, forcing them to over-grow as insurance against under-selling. Meanwhile, farm-to-table restaurants that want to source locally cannot plan their menus more than 48 hours in advance because farm availability updates are communicated informally and inconsistently. A B2B marketplace where farms list weekly available inventory with 7-day forward visibility and restaurants place standing or one-time orders with delivery routing can eliminate 80% of the phone-and-email coordination overhead on both sides.
target_users: Independent restaurant owners and executive chefs at farm-to-table restaurants that source 30%+ of produce locally and spend significant time on supplier coordination
Food co-op purchasing managers who place weekly bulk produce orders from 5-15 farms and track delivery schedules across a spreadsheet
Small to mid-size farm operators (5-500 acres) within 150 miles of a major metro area who sell to restaurants but lack the digital infrastructure to post availability or receive online orders
Regional food distributors who aggregate farm supply for last-mile delivery and want a digital order consolidation tool to replace phone order intake
user_stories: As an executive chef, I want to browse available produce from all farms within 100 miles filtered by item, quantity, and earliest delivery date so that I can build my menu 5 days in advance instead of 48 hours
As a farm operator, I want to post my available harvest quantities for the coming week by Sunday evening so that restaurant buyers see my inventory when they plan their orders on Monday morning
As a restaurant purchasing manager, I want to place a standing weekly order for a specific quantity of an item that auto-renews unless I cancel so that I don't re-order routine items every week
As a farm operator, I want to receive aggregated order totals by item by midnight Sunday so that I know exactly what to harvest on Monday and can minimize field waste

As a food co-op purchasing manager, I want a single consolidated delivery manifest for all farms in a given week sorted by delivery date so that I can coordinate receiving without cross-referencing five separate emails
As a restaurant owner, I want to rate each delivery on freshness and accuracy (1-5 stars) within 24 hours of receipt so that other buyers can see the farm's quality track record before ordering

As a farm operator, I want to send an availability update to all buyers with pending orders for a specific item with a single broadcast message so that buyers can adjust their orders without individual calls
acceptance_criteria: Farm operators can post available inventory (item name, variety, quantity in lbs or units, unit price, earliest available date, and notes) for the coming 7 days via web or mobile; inventory is visible to restaurant buyers within 5 minutes of posting

Restaurants can search available inventory by item, farm, distance (up to 150 miles from restaurant zip code), and earliest delivery date; search results return within 2 seconds for a catalog of up to 500 active farm listings

Standing orders are created with item, quantity, frequency (weekly or biweekly), and delivery day; they generate a confirmed order automatically each cycle unless the restaurant cancels at least 48 hours before the delivery day or the farm's inventory for that item is exhausted

Farm operators receive a consolidated order summary (total units per item across all buyers) at midnight on the order cutoff day (configurable, default Sunday); the summary is sent via email and in-app notification

Delivery manifests are generated per restaurant per week, listing all ordered items, farms, quantities, unit prices, total, and confirmed delivery date; manifests update automatically if a farm adjusts availability

Farm quality ratings (1-5 stars, plus optional text) submitted within 24 hours of a marked delivery are published on the farm's profile within 1 hour of submission; the farm's rolling 90-day average rating is displayed on all their inventory listings

Farm availability broadcast messages reach all buyers with pending orders for the affected item within 10 minutes of the farm sending the message; buyers with affected orders see an in-app alert and can modify or cancel within 12 hours at no penalty
HarvestLink processes payments via Stripe; farms receive payouts within 3 business days of a delivery being marked complete by the restaurant, minus the 8% platform fee disclosed at farm onboarding

success_metrics.metric: Gross merchandise volume (total value of produce orders transacted through HarvestLink per month)
success_metrics.baseline: $0 at launch; TAM estimate: $2.1B in local farm-to-restaurant direct sales in top 10 US metro areas
success_metrics.target: $500K monthly GMV within 12 months of launch in the first metro market (Portland, OR)

success_metrics.metric: Farm produce waste rate (percentage of posted harvest quantity that goes unsold through HarvestLink, self-reported by farm operators at end of week)
success_metrics.baseline: Estimated 18% waste rate based on pre-launch interviews with 15 farm operators
success_metrics.target: Average farm produce waste rate below 8% within 6 months of farm onboarding

success_metrics.metric: Buyer weekly order frequency (average number of weeks per month a restaurant account places at least one order)
success_metrics.target: Average of 3.5 weeks per month for restaurant accounts active for 60+ days

success_metrics.metric: Standing order adoption rate (percentage of active restaurant accounts that have at least one active standing order)
success_metrics.target: 55% of restaurant accounts active for 30+ days have at least one standing order by month 6

success_metrics.metric: Farm onboarding rate (farms that post available inventory at least once in their first 14 days after account creation)
success_metrics.target: 70% farm activation rate within 3 months of launch

risks_open_questions: Cold-start supply-demand problem: restaurants won't order without farm supply, and farms won't post without buyer demand — need to pre-sign 15+ farms and 20+ restaurant buyers before launching in the first metro market
Farm internet connectivity: many small farm operators work from mobile and may have poor connectivity in fields; the mobile posting interface must work on 3G and handle offline draft saving

Food safety liability: if a buyer receives contaminated produce ordered through HarvestLink, the platform's role in the supply chain creates potential legal exposure; need terms of service and liability framework reviewed by legal before launch

Delivery logistics: HarvestLink connects buyers and farms but does not operate delivery in v1; if farms cannot reliably deliver, order fulfillment breaks down — need to vet farm delivery capability at onboarding
Produce grading standards: 'heirloom tomatoes' means different quality grades to different farms; need a minimum description standard (including grade where applicable) to reduce buyer disputes
Seasonality: in northern markets, farm activity drops 60%+ in winter months — what is the strategy to retain restaurant buyers during low-supply periods to prevent churn?

How should HarvestLink handle order disputes (wrong quantity delivered, quality below listing description) — is the platform the mediator, or does it stay out of disputes beyond facilitating communication?
out_of_scope: Operating delivery vehicles or last-mile logistics in v1; farms arrange their own delivery or use existing regional distributors
Consumer-facing marketplace (B2C); HarvestLink is B2B only in v1
Meat, dairy, or non-produce farm categories at launch (fresh produce only)
Integration with restaurant POS systems or food cost management platforms
USDA organic certification verification or food safety audit documentation
Multi-metro launch; Portland, OR is the only market at launch
Financing or net-30 payment terms for restaurant buyers; all orders are prepaid at checkout
